% The reported case: an ENGLISH document with one Hebrew run in it, which is what the report
% actually is. Hebrew forces luaotfload onto the HarfBuzz renderer (harfloaded: filename), and
% the run sits in a TRT box inside an otherwise left-to-right line -- so the page has to come
% back uncertified as "dir" on the strength of that nested box alone.
% and bidi=default makes the boxes TRT, so the page must come back uncertified as "dir".
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[main=english, bidi=default]{babel}
\babelprovide[import]{hebrew}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{Times New Roman}
\babelfont[hebrew]{rm}{Times New Roman}
\begin{document}
This is a test for \foreignlanguage{hebrew}{עברית}.
\end{document}
